children: Koppers’ third-quarter sales rose 2.8% year over year, while earnings declined. Higher volume in Performance Chemicals, Class I crossties and domestic utility poles drove sales growth; lower crosstie pricing, higher raw material and logistics costs, and weaker results in Carbon Materials and Chemicals weighed on profitability.
¹ Reported as “Net sales”. ² Reported as “Net income (loss)”. ³ Reported as “Diluted”.
: Sales rose 11.9% as volume increased 10%, primarily in the Americas, on market-share gains and inventory restocking.
Railroad and Utility Products and Services
: Domestic utility-pole volume increased 5%; adjusted EBITDA fell to $22.3M, chiefly on lower crosstie pricing and higher costs.
: Adjusted EBITDA declined to $6.1M amid higher raw material costs and lower utilization tied to feedstock quality and the accelerated Stickney closure.
: Koppers discontinued distillation and chemical production activities in October and shifted production to its Nyborg, Denmark facility.
